observational_dataset.appendix_b_likelihood: arXiv:1805.02016v2 Table I, with the table's quoted mass/spin estimates and confidence levels
observational_dataset.reference_2021_analytic_plot: arXiv:2009.07206v1 Fig. 3, fixed scalar mass 4.3e-12 eV, stellar mass panel, l=m=1..5, tau=1e10 yr and 4.5e6 yr
observational_dataset.reason: Appendix B assumes Gaussian mass and spin uncertainties but Table I contains one-sided spin bounds and mixed asymmetric/confidence-level errors. The source does not define a conversion of censored or mixed-confidence entries into the required sigma values, nor a complete source subset for which all required sigmas are given. Do not infer symmetric errors, drop rows, or produce authoritative source-wide P_allowed/P_ex.

units_and_constants.external_inputs: BH mass in solar masses; scalar mass in eV; spin dimensionless; time in years; quartic lambda dimensionless in natural units; f_pert in GeV
units_and_constants.source_spin_change_for_Nmax: Delta_a_star=0.1, the normalization used in Eq. (9); Nmax = G*M_BH^2*Delta_a_star/(m*hbar*c), where m is the azimuthal integer, not the boson mass.

reference_analytic_method.rate: 2020 Eq. (12)-(14), with n_r in A_nl and N=n_r+l+1; evaluate in geometric units and convert inverse geometric length to s^-1

source_plot_mass_grid.interpolation: none; solve each grid point directly

reference_analytic_method.source_support: Only the source's Fig. 3 fixed-mass stellar panel (0.1..100 solar masses) is used for the bounded plot reconstruction. Preserve the source analytic approximation as written; report its low-alpha qualification and do not extrapolate the generated table beyond the fixed source panel.
reference_analytic_method.mode_envelope: The exclusion region is the union of the per-mode source instability regions. Keep per-mode boundaries and the union as separate outputs.

appendix_b_likelihood_method.equations: Eqs. (95)-(98), zero x-y covariance, effective one-dimensional projected errors, direct/inverse branches, nearest inverse branch derivative, erf interval between inverse branches, conservative total-contour cusp behavior
appendix_b_likelihood_method.derivative: 5-point centered finite difference in the source coordinate, step=1e-5 times max(1,abs(coordinate)); one-sided second-order difference at support boundaries
appendix_b_likelihood_method.inverse: bracketed bisection on each monotone contour branch; absolute residual tolerance 1e-12 in source coordinate
appendix_b_likelihood_method.likelihood_grid: reuse 1201-point log-mass grid and direct spin roots; no extrapolation
appendix_b_likelihood_method.data_gate: Fail closed on a missing, censored, or confidence-level-ambiguous sigma. Source-wide Appendix-B probability is unavailable until every required data row has a source-defined sigma or the source explicitly defines a complete subset.

bosenova_method.Nmax: 2020 Eq. (9), Delta_a_star=0.1 normalization, mode azimuthal m in denominator
bosenova_method.NBose: 2021 Eq. (13): 1e78*cBose*N^4/alpha^3*(M_BH/(10 M_sun))^2*(f_pert/M_Pl)^2, with cBose=5 and principal N from source_mode_manifest
bosenova_method.fpert: sqrt(mu^2/abs(lambda_iiii)); preserve signed lambda provenance, use its absolute value in criterion
bosenova_method.efficiency_condition: 2020 Eq. (26): Gamma_SR*tau_BH*(NBose/Nmax) > ln(NBose); equality is the regression transition boundary
bosenova_method.data_gate: Formula-level results for named inputs only; no source-wide probability product without authoritative Appendix-B inputs.

continued_fraction_method.convergence_acceptance: last two precision/order refinements change omega*M and Gamma*M by at most 1e-8 relative; compare converged Gamma with the REFERENCE_2021_ANALYTIC low-alpha Eq. (12)-(14) value without fitting constants
continued_fraction_method.authority: validation only; never relabel CF output as REFERENCE_2021_ANALYTIC
